defects.claim: Gambler's ruin table: 'the probability of hitting zero within n duels from a bankroll of k stake-units is: k=1: 75% in 2 duels, 88% in 10; k=2: 25% / 73%; ...'
defects.problem: Recomputed by exact DP (p=0.5, win nets +0.8 stake after a 10% pot fee). The quoted figures are NOT the probability of hitting zero; they only appear if 'ruin' means 'balance falls below one stake unit of the chosen tier'. Hitting zero from k=1 in 2 duels is 50%, not 75%; k=1/n=10 is 79.5%, not 88%; k=5/n=10 is 10.9%, not 22%. Even under the below-one-unit definition, k=2/n=10 recomputes to 68.6%, not 73% (no definition tried reproduces 73%).
defects.correction: Relabel the table as 'probability of no longer affording the same tier' and fix k=2/n=10 to about 69%; or, if the design intent really is 'hits zero', replace the whole row set with 50/79.5/25/54.9/34.4/10.9/34.2/0.1/3.4.

defects.claim: 'at any eCPM_IN below about $5.5 the floor rule R_g >= s_min = 10 binds, so India pays 10 coins per ad'
defects.problem: With R_g = max(10, round5(50 x eCPM/27.32)) the reward is 10 coins for every eCPM up to about $6.83 (raw < 12.5), and the max() floor itself only binds when round5() would return 5 or 0, i.e. eCPM below about $4.10. $5.5 is neither threshold.
defects.correction: State the outcome threshold as about $6.8 (below which India pays 10 coins) and the true floor-binding threshold as about $4.1.

defects.claim: Steady-state balance 'B* = F / (n_d x r x phi) = 100 / (2 x 0.10 x 0.10) = 5,000 coins - which is exactly the current soft cap, so the two mechanisms agree'
defects.problem: The brief's own per-session faucet total (same finding set) is F = 116, not 100, which gives B* = 5,800. Also phi = 0.10 at B = 5,000 means a 500-coin stake, a tier the brief says is only unlocked ABOVE the soft cap and carries a 15% fee under its own escalation schedule, so the 'exact agreement' with the 5,000 soft cap is an artefact of the chosen inputs, not a result.
defects.correction: Recompute with consistent inputs (F=116, and the fee/tier actually reachable below the cap) and present B* as a rough order-of-magnitude, not as confirming the soft cap.

defects.claim: Arena fee schedule: finding 7 says '10% on the pot at tiers >= 1 AE, 0% at the two micro tiers'; finding 8 lever (2) says 'fee escalates with tier (5% at 1 AE, 10% at 2-5 AE, 15% at 10 AE)'; recommendation 2 says '10% of the pot at 50-250, 15% at a new 500 tier'
defects.problem: Three mutually inconsistent fee schedules for the 50-coin (1 AE) tier: 10%, 5% and 10%. The inflation accounting (10 coins of fee from 2 duels at 1 AE) uses 10%, which contradicts the 5% in the same finding's control levers.
defects.correction: Pick one schedule and propagate it through the break-even, inflation and B* arithmetic.

defects.claim: 'target sinks/faucets >= 0.35 at launch rising to 0.6 by month 3'
defects.problem: The brief's own base case is 37 sinks / 116 faucets = 0.32, which already misses the launch target it sets.
defects.correction: Either lower the launch target to about 0.3 or add sink volume to the base case before stating the target.

defects.claim: 'Kelly for an even-money bet is f* = 2p - 1, which is 0 at p=0.5 - there is no positive-EV stake for a median player'
defects.problem: The duel is not even-money once a 10% pot fee exists: a win nets +0.8 stake, so Kelly is f* = p/l - q/g = 0.5 - 0.5/0.8 = -0.125 at p=0.5 (negative, i.e. do not bet). The conclusion survives but the stated formula does not apply to the designed game.
defects.correction: Use f* = p - (1-p)/0.8 and state that it is negative for any p below 5/9.

defects.claim: Q2 2024 rewarded eCPM by country (Tenjin/CAS.AI) 'verified' from chart images iOS_Rewarded-3.png and Android_Rewarded-4.png
defects.problem: The chart values match what the images show and the page captions them 'Q2 2024', but both files live in the WordPress upload folder /wp-content/uploads/2024/05/ (uploaded May 2024, before Q2 2024 ended) and the page's own methodology window is 01.01.2024-30.06.2024. The report text never quantifies these numbers; provenance rests solely on a caption whose date is inconsistent with the file's upload date.
defects.correction: Downgrade to 'likely' and note the upload-date discrepancy; treat the table as H1-2024 CAS.AI data of uncertain quarter.

defects.claim: 'rewarded ad max duration 30 s (60 s with high-engagement ads) per https://support.google.com/admob/answer/7311747'
defects.problem: The AdMob page says 'The maximum length to skip a rewarded ad is 30 seconds. If high-engagement ads are enabled, the maximum length to skip a rewarded ad is 60 seconds.' That is the latest point at which the skip/reward gate can sit, not a maximum ad duration.
defects.correction: Describe it as the maximum time-to-skip (reward point); the 30-45 s per-ad assumption in the farm-vs-ad comparison should be labelled an assumption.

defects.claim: Google SSV rationale quoted as 'applications where reward validity is critical (for example, the reward affects your app's in-game economy)'
defects.problem: The full sentence is 'for applications where reward validity is critical ... and delays in granting rewards are acceptable, waiting for the verified server-side callback may be the best approach.' The brief drops the 'delays ... are acceptable' qualifier, which is material to the recommendation to pay only on verified receipts (UX latency).
defects.correction: Quote the full condition and address the reward-delay UX in the recommendation.

defects.claim: Sensor Tower report landing page https://sensortower.com/blog/gaming-deep-dive-ad-monetization-report (June 2026, figures gated) cited alongside DoF's 3 Aug 2025 read of 'Sensor Tower's 2025 ad-monetisation report'
defects.problem: The DoF article (verified: Josh Chandley, 3 Aug 2025) discusses the 2025 edition; the Sensor Tower page cited is the June 2026 edition (author Bryan Isagholian). The 2025 figures are sourced only via DoF; the ST link does not corroborate them.
defects.correction: Cite the DoF post alone for the 2025 numbers, or link the 2025 edition of the ST report.

defects.claim: 'Lehdonvirta & Castronova, Virtual Economies: Design and Analysis (MIT Press, 2014, ISBN 0262535068)'
defects.problem: ISBN 0262535068 (978-0262535069) is the 2018 MIT Press paperback; the 2014 hardcover is ISBN 9780262027250. Year and ISBN do not match one edition.

defects.claim: US blended rewarded eCPM $27.32 = mean of iOS $24.39 and Android $30.25
defects.problem: An unweighted mean; the same Tenjin page gives a 55% Android / 45% iOS ad-revenue split, and impression weighting is unknown. The anchor value (and every derived coin rate) shifts by up to about 3 cents per coin-thousand depending on weighting.
defects.correction: Say 'simple mean' explicitly and note sensitivity, or weight by the product's expected platform mix (a web app has neither).

Streaks: P(LLL within 4) = 3/16 = 18.75%; P(>=3-run of L in 10) = 1 - 504/1024 = 50.8% (match)
